per_target_result.behavioral_obligation: a non-empty but malformed contract_id must fail closed
per_target_result.honest_analysis: STRUCTURALLY_UNREACHABLE via this function's own control flow, confirmed by direct source reading. Before the mutated `_SAFE_CONTRACT_ID.fullmatch(contract_id)` check is ever reached, an EARLIER, unconditional check (`if contract_id != authorized_contract_id: raise ...`) already requires contract_id to be EXACTLY equal to the hardcoded, well-formed `_AUTHORIZED_INPUT_CONTRACT_ID_BY_PROFILE[feature_computation_profile]` value (itself derived from `_INPUT_CONTRACT_RELPATHS`, always a well-formed path stem). By the time execution reaches the mutated line, contract_id is therefore provably always well-formed already -- the `_SAFE_CONTRACT_ID.fullmatch` check can never actually fail for any value that survives the prior binding check. Killing this would require either a production-code change (weakening the `_AUTHORIZED_INPUT_CONTRACT_ID_BY_PROFILE` binding, or reordering the checks) or an impossible fixture (a malformed value that is simultaneously bit-for-bit equal to a known well-formed authorized constant) -- both explicitly prohibited by this WP. Reported honestly, not gamed.

per_target_result.behavioral_obligation: multi-part identity composition must preserve part boundaries / use the exact documented algorithm
per_target_result.honest_analysis: First attempt (boundary-shift inequality, deterministic_id('ab','c') != deterministic_id('a','bc')) was independently verified via fresh diff extraction to NOT distinguish this specific mutation: the mutant WIDENS the separator from '|' to 'XX|XX' rather than narrowing/removing it, so boundary-shift inequality still holds under both the real and mutated separator (a wider unique separator does not reintroduce a collision). The mutation was killed instead via a determinism/stability pin: two exact SHA-256 digests (independently computed with the real '|' separator) asserted for known two- and three-part inputs -- this validates the module's own documented 'same parts always produce the same id' stability guarantee at a concrete, verifiable value, and is sensitive to any silent change of the join algorithm (including this exact separator-widening mutation). This is a legitimate golden-value regression test on a hash function's own documented determinism contract, not a message-text or mutant-identity assertion.
